title: Runtime API Stabilization Charter and Migration Signal Framework
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Goal: define a pragmatic, audit-friendly semantic versioning and LTS channel policy for the runtime that minimizes customer disruption while enabling safe evolution. Deliver a classified change matrix (Breaking / Behavior-change / Additive), explicit deprecation signal headers, and a migration signal framework consumed by CI/CD and the upgrade CLI. This charter covers: version number semantics tied to API/ABI, how LTS branches are created and maintained, automated rollout gate checks, required release artifacts, and the migration helper tool contract.
acceptance_criteria: Publish a one-page runtime semver charter and public FAQ for customers
Implement 'X-Redwood-Deprecation' and 'X-Redwood-Breaking' response headers in runtime for 3 months before major bump
Ship an automated compatibility-checker in CI that emits clear pass/warn/fail signals for compatibility categories
Add a migration-signal hook to the upgrade CLI that surfaces concrete steps (config flags, config migrations, CVEs)
Define LTS eligibility rules and automated gating for cherry-picked backports
plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Draft charter, change taxonomy, and example compatibility matrix; review with Runtime and API teams
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement response headers and server-side change classifier; add compatibility-checker job in CI
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Extend upgrade CLI to consume classifier output and emit step-by-step migration hints; integrate with Console release notes
Phase 4 (1 week): Run a canary on a small set of internal customers, collect telemetry, iterate on gate thresholds
rollout_gates: Unit and integration tests: 100% pass for minor/patch; breaking changes require explicit approval
Compatibility-checker warnings must be triaged and documented before canary
Canary period: 72 hours with no increase in 5xx rate and token-latency regressions <5%
Rollout pause if customer-facing errors exceed threshold or upgrade-scripts fail on >1% of canary hosts
telemetry: Track X-Redwood-Deprecation header occurrences and most common stack traces by customer
Latency and 5xx histograms per model/model-variant during canary
Record upgrade failures from upgrade CLI (exit code, failed step, host)
migration_tooling: upgrade-cli: new 'analyze-release' command that consumes CI classifier output and generates a migration playbook
compatibility-checker: runs on PR and release branch, emits machine-readable report and human summary
deprecation-notifier: scheduled job that emails customers with active usage of deprecated endpoints
automated-backport-bot: suggests backport PRs for LTS branches when fixes are labeled 'backport-candidate'
rollback_plan: If canary or early rollout triggers a gate, the controller will stop the rollout and perform an automatic rollback to the previous runtime artifact. Rollback steps are: mark release as 'paused', trigger autoscaler to drain new pods, redeploy previous release, run smoke checks, notify on-call and affected customers. Post-mortem required within 48 hours.
notes: Trade-offs: stricter gating reduces incidents but slows feature velocity; charter recommends a two-track approach: fast path for additive changes, strict path for behavioral/breaking changes
Policy nuance: not all major version bumps must be accompanied by code removal; we allow 'compatibility-mode' flags to defer breakage for one LTS cycle when feasible
Customer comms: include changelog snippets and migration hints in release notes; provide opt-in preview channels for enterprise customers
